en.title: Ways to Form a Fleet with Two-Wheelers and Four-Wheelers
en.description:
Two-wheel and four-wheel vehicles are available in unlimited supply. For each total number of wheels, count the distinct combinations of the numbers of the two vehicle types.

The standard I/O and the solution were written independently by this site; ranges marked as this site's are not the original source constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n (1..100000), and the second line contains n wheel totals (1..10⁹).
en.output: Output n integers in input order.
en.explanation: Example 1: 6 has the two options (3,0) and (1,1), 3 has no solution, and 2 has only (1,0), so output 2 0 1. Example 2: 4 and 6 have two options each, and 5 has no solution. Example 3: 1 has no solution; 8 has three options with 0, 1 or 2 four-wheelers, so output 0 3.
hints: Odd totals have no solution; for even totals the number of four-wheelers can be 0 to w//4, and the remaining wheels uniquely determine the number of two-wheelers.
